applicablePercentage.source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25 §3.01, 'Applicable Percentage Table for 2026' (taxable years beginning in calendar year 2026). ✓ PRIMARY READ DISCHARGED 2026-08-01 and INDEPENDENTLY RE-READ 2026-08-02: irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-25.pdf was fetched twice on separate passes and its §3.01 table extracted by TWO different engines (pdftotext -layout, and PyMuPDF word-geometry which reconstructs columns from x/y coordinates rather than from spacing) — both agree cell-for-cell. These figures are transcribed FROM THAT DOCUMENT, never from health.ts — howToClear step 6, so the bind stays non-circular. The table verbatim, six rows, Initial/Final: 'Less than 133%' 2.10/2.10 · 'At least 133% but less than 150%' 3.14/4.19 · 'At least 150% but less than 200%' 4.19/6.60 · 'At least 200% but less than 250%' 6.60/8.44 · 'At least 250% but less than 300%' 8.44/9.96 · 'At least 300% but not more than 400%' 9.96/9.96. Each row's Final equals the next row's Initial, which is the table's own internal chain and a cheap transcription check. §3.02 additionally gives the Required Contribution Percentage for plan years beginning in 2026 as 9.96%. DISCRIMINATING PROOF (per DND 012 — 9.96% alone is published identically in BOTH regimes and proves nothing): the table's SHAPE. It terminates at 'not more than 400%' and floors at 2.10%, which is the REVERTED regime; the enhanced 2021-2025 table has no 400% cap and floors at 0.00%. ⚠️ But see discriminatingProof entry 4: the SHAPE identifies the regime the document was DRAFTED under, and a Rev. Proc. is a LAGGING indicator of the statute — this attestation pins the figures the engine prices with, not the legislative status.

THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING LEG. The granule's own Amendments notes show the last touch to EITHER provision was Pub. L. 117-169 §12001 (2022), and the last law to amend §36B at all is Pub. L. 119-21 (2025-07-04), whose seven 2025 amendments touch (c)(1)(B), (c)(3)(A), (c)(5)-(6), (e)(1), (e)(2) and (f)(2) — none of them (b)(3)(A)(iii) or (c)(1)(E).

THE CURRENCY MARKER IS PER-TITLE, AND THE PRIOR RECORD DID NOT KNOW THAT. The §36B granule reads 'currentthrough:20260413_119-83', which reads like a ceiling of PL 119-83 and is NOT one: control fetches on 2026-08-02 show 26 USC 1, 26 USC 35, 26 USC 5000A ALL carry the same 119-83 stamp while 42 USC 18071 carries 20260712_119-102 — so the marker is a per-TITLE regeneration stamp, not a verification ceiling. OLRC's currency page states the operative rule ('If there are no pending updates listed, the section is current as shown') and §36B renders NO pending-update element. Corroborated independently by the OLRC Classification Tables: the 119th/2nd table (PL 119-70 and 119-74 through 119-102) has ZERO '36B' rows against a working positive control — the 119th/1st table has nine, all attributed to 119-21. Net: §36B is verified unaffected through PL 119-102, not merely through 119-83.

NO ENACTED LAW TOUCHES §36B. All 19 public laws from 119-84 through 119-102 were retrieved from govinfo with REAL bodies and full-text swept for '36B', 'premium tax credit', 'premium assistance', '9661', '9662', 'applicable percentage': ZERO hits in every one. The zero is non-vacuous on two guards — a positive control ('Congress assembled') fires in all 19, and the sweep was re-run with whitespace flattened because govinfo hard-wraps at ~72 columns and a multi-word phrase can split across a newline. Pub. L. 119-98 (S. 2) is a RECONCILIATION act — historically THE vehicle for ACA subsidy changes — so it was cleared structurally as well as by keyword: its entire contents are TITLE I (Homeland Security) and TITLE II (Judiciary), and credit/health/insurance/subsid/exchange all count zero against firing controls.

⚠️ CORROBORATIVE ONLY — AND DELIBERATELY DEMOTED 2026-08-02 FROM THE 'AFFIRMATIVE PROOF' IT WAS FILED AS. Rev. Proc. 2026-26 (IRB 2026-31, 2026-07-27, p.131) publishes the TY2027 table in the SAME reverted shape — floor 2.15%, terminating at 'At least 300% but not more than 400% — 10.22%', Required Contribution Percentage 10.22% — re-read on 2026-08-02 from irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-26-26.pdf by two independent extraction engines. THE CLAIM THIS ENTRY USED TO MAKE IS FALSE: it read 'Treasury could not have published that shape if the enhanced schedule had been restored.' Treasury demonstrably could, and did. COUNTEREXAMPLE, FULLY PRIMARY: Rev. Proc. 2022-34 published the TY2023 table in exactly this reverted shape (floor 1.92%, terminating at '300% but not more than 400% — 9.12%', six bands) in IRB 2022-33 dated 2022-08-15 — and the Inflation Reduction Act was enacted the NEXT DAY, 2022-08-16 (PLAW-117publ169, '<<NOTE: Aug. 16, 2022>>'), §12001 extending the enhanced schedule through 2025. That published table never operated for a single taxpayer, and the IRS never retracted it (Rev. Proc. 2023-29 §3 'EFFECT ON OTHER DOCUMENTS' supplements only Rev. Proc. 2014-37). A Rev. Proc. is a LAGGING indicator: it reports the regime the drafters were under on the posting date. And the lag here is far worse than one day — rp-25-25.pdf, the table THIS engine prices with, has Last-Modified 2025-07-17, i.e. it was posted before the expiration it describes had even occurred and before the entire 2026 legislative session. It carries zero information about a 2026 restoration. It corroborates the statute; it cannot substitute for it.

AFFIRMATIVE, EXECUTIVE-BRANCH, IN-WINDOW — the leg that replaces the demoted one, and the first time this record has carried it. HHS's own final rule says the subsidies expired. 'HHS Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters for 2027', Federal Register doc 2026-10050, published 2026-05-20, retrieved in full text 2026-08-02, states verbatim: 'many resources needed to implement and oversee administration of the enhanced subsidies codified under the ARP, and later extended under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, are no longer needed since they expired at the end of 2025.' It also prices the reverted world operatively — 'For individuals with household income above 400 percent of the FPL who are ineligible for APTC, the full unsubsidized premium cost … may or may not exceed the affordability exemption threshold.' Corroborated by live IRS consumer guidance (irs.gov Q&A on the premium tax credit, Q7 stamped '(updated Feb. 19, 2026)' — i.e. re-touched AFTER the House passed its extension on 2026-01-08 and after the Senate calendared it on 02-10): 'no more than 400 percent of the federal poverty line … For tax years 2021 through 2025, Congress temporarily expanded eligibility'. Past tense, after the vote. This is an agency ACTING on the expiration, which is a different kind of evidence from a table's shape.

howToClear: Re-verify the CURRENT ACA enhanced-subsidy status against an enacted statute / IRS notice, then update verifiedOn + status + summary. Do NOT just bump the date — the law can flip the whole pre-65 model. Budget ~1 hour; the chain below is the one that works, each link independent. (1) Read §36B(b)(3)(A)(iii) and (c)(1)(E) at uscode.house.gov and note the granule's currentthrough marker — ⚠️ that marker is PER-TITLE and is NOT a verification ceiling (Title 26 read 119-83 while Title 42 read 119-102 on the same day); the operative rule is OLRC's own: no pending-update element means the section is current as shown, and the Classification Tables are the independent check. (2) Full-text sweep every public law above the real ceiling from govinfo, checking BODIES not status codes, with a positive control and a whitespace-flattened re-run (govinfo hard-wraps at ~72 columns, so a multi-word phrase can split and yield a false ZERO). (3) Confirm the law ceiling the same way, and cross-check archives.gov/federal-register/laws/current. (4) Check congress.gov presented-to-president.xml is empty — and read that leg as a BOUND on last-hours risk, not as proof. (5) Find the newest Rev. Proc. applicable-percentage table and confirm whether it terminates at 400%. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-02 — THE PRIOR VERSION OF THIS STEP SAID IT WAS 'AFFIRMATIVE EVIDENCE AND WORTH MORE THAN ANY NUMBER OF ABSENT-NEWS SEARCHES.' THAT IS FALSE and the counterexample is in discriminatingProof entry 4: Rev. Proc. 2022-34 published a reverted-shape table the day before the IRA restored the enhanced one. The Rev. Proc. LAGS the statute, so step 5 CORROBORATES; steps 1-3 are what prove. A re-verify that checks only step 5 has a documented one-day-miss failure mode. (6) RE-TYPE attests.applicablePercentage FROM the Rev. Proc. you opened in step 5, by hand, NEVER by copying src/engine/constants/health.ts. That table is re-issued ANNUALLY and clause (ii) indexing applies to it, so a new Rev. Proc. silently supersedes the shipped one; the bind arms in scripts/__tests__/verify-aca-status.test.ts compare your transcription against the constant and go RED on a one-sided edit. Copying from the constant makes that bind circular and defeats the gate. attests.enhancedPercentage is FIXED statute (clause (ii) does not apply) and only moves if Congress acts — but re-type it from the §36B granule you already have open in step 1, NOT from the constant: that attestation was circular until 2026-08-02 and said so in its own source line. (7) Check the Federal Register API (documents.json, publication_date ≥ the year start) for 'enhanced premium tax credit' and '36B' — a restoration forces agency rulemaking, so this is cheap negative space, and HHS's annual Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters states the operative posture in plain language. (8) Every citation you write down must be retrieved and opened — see strickenCitations, both classes.
